summary: The session discusses the evolving landscape of data integration, emphasizing the continued relevance of ETL alongside emerging trends such as streaming and ontology-driven integration. It highlights best practices for organizations to enhance their integration maturity, including the adoption of minimum lovable products and self-service capabilities. The speaker also introduces a data integration maturity framework to guide organizations in optimizing their data integration strategies.

key_points: ETL is still relevant due to ongoing organizational needs for data movement.
Emerging technologies include zero ETL, streaming integration, and ontology-driven integration.
Organizations should focus on developing minimum lovable products to validate business value.
Self-service capabilities should be enabled while maintaining governance and oversight.
Adopt a data integration maturity framework to assess and enhance integration capabilities.
Focus on balancing integration styles and optimizing costs through effective governance.

key_takeaways: ETL remains a critical component of data integration despite emerging technologies.
Organizations should prioritize minimum lovable products to ensure alignment with business needs.
Implementing a data integration maturity framework can guide organizations towards enhanced integration capabilities.
